# WhereDNS 0.2

WhereDNS 0.2 makes DNS behavior and defensive security concepts visible as interactive, step-by-step sequence diagrams while preserving the standalone native CLI.

## Highlights

- Visualize recursive DNS interrogations as actor-to-actor exchanges with status, transport, timing, packet size, record-section counts, and DNSSEC context.
- See explicit WhereDNS cache lookups, misses, stores, and cache hits without misrepresenting cached data as network traffic.
- Follow direct iterative traces as separate root, TLD, and authoritative question/response pairs, including mixed cache and network provenance.
- Explore all nineteen DNS attack families through structured actor graphs that distinguish normal protocol traffic, trust-boundary warnings, malicious paths, and defensive controls.
- Reuse the matching threat visualization inside each linked safe laboratory exercise.
- Select numbered events for detailed explanations with keyboard support and a color-independent text reader.
- Use the responsive graph canvas on desktop or mobile without page-level horizontal overflow.

## Data and compatibility

- The CLI remains the primary standalone application and all existing commands remain available.
- Trace JSON steps now expose `from_cache`, `transport`, and `response_bytes` so other interfaces can accurately represent what occurred.
- Attack JSON entries now include a structured `flow` containing actors and events.

## Safety

Attack diagrams remain conceptual and defensive. They do not add spoofing, flooding, external mutation, or unrestricted resolver-abuse capabilities. Live laboratory services remain loopback-only.

## Release assets

Archives are provided for Linux and macOS on AMD64/ARM64, and Windows on AMD64. Verify downloads with `SHA256SUMS`.

See the [README](https://github.com/MinottiAlessandro/WhereDNS#readme) for usage, feature boundaries, and responsible-use guidance.
